analysis:
Reviewed the CI workflow change in .github/workflows/provider-tests.yml. It is CI scheduling and artifact bookkeeping only; no provider runtime, coordinator contract, key handling, attestation, encryption or prefix-cache code changes. No threat-model asset (A-001..A-020), boundary or threat (including T-041 cache storage, T-053, T-054) is touched.

Changes seen: (1) a new required workflow_call input `cluster_gpu`; the GPU cluster job (test-cluster-gpu, base ~line 922) is now gated on it instead of `inputs.cluster`. It is non-blocking and continue-on-error, so a skipped GPU lane reduces test coverage but not any security gate. (2) The push-time cache-refresh build path (`skip == 'true' && changed_*`) is removed from build-cluster and build-provider, so a push of an already-tested tree now skips builds. This cannot affect shipped artifacts because it only touches CI test products and caches. (3) The tested-change record step now also emits a tree-record artifact via `ci-tested-tree.py tree-name`, and both uploads use `overwrite: true`. The `name`/`tree_name` values come from a repo script, and the inputs $TREE/$BASE/$HEAD are passed through env vars, not interpolated into the shell script, so there is no script injection. The overwrite flag lets a later run replace a same-named record artifact. That record is used by provider-plan.yml and the scripts to decide whether a tree is already tested and to skip testing. Whether the tree-name binds to the exact tree and component set, and whether a PR run can poison a record that a push run later trusts, depends on scripts/ci-tested-tree.py, provider-plan.yml, ci-dev.yml and ci-master.yml, which were not supplied. This is an unverified contract and I make no finding. Permissions remain contents: read, and the action pins are unchanged.

Remaining integration questions: how provider-plan.yml computes `cluster_gpu` and `skip`, how callers pass the new required input, and whether the tree-record artifact lookup is bound to the trusted tree and components. The patch excerpt was truncated at the tail but the range map is complete.
